title: Custom managed-pages layouts get escaped parts only
detail: A custom `wrapLayout` used to receive the page title, description, language, slug, OG image and the tenant branding raw, and was trusted to escape them itself; a naive template string turned a tenant admin's branding title into markup on the public page. It now receives `bodyHtml`, `titleHtml`, `descriptionHtml`, `langHtml`, `slugHtml`, `ogImageHtml` (empty unless it is an https URL), `brandingStyleHtml` (theme variables plus the sanitized tenant CSS) and `brandingHeaderHtml`, all escaped or sanitized, so every field can be interpolated as is. The default layout is unchanged.
migration: Rewrite a custom managed-pages `wrapLayout` to the new fields: `title` becomes `titleHtml`, `lang` becomes `langHtml`, `description` becomes `descriptionHtml`, and `brandingStyleBlock(o.branding)`, `tenantStyleBlock(o.branding.customCss)` and `brandingHeaderHtml(o.branding)` become `o.brandingStyleHtml` and `o.brandingHeaderHtml`. Keep `TENANT_CONTENT_ATTR` on the content container.

title: One validation for page slug, language and OG image
Published page list no longer loads page bodies
Published page list always reads the caller's tenant
detail: The discovery query accepted a tenantIdOverride that could never reach another tenant through the tenant-scoped read. The field is gone; the query lists the published pages of the caller's tenant.
migration: Drop tenantIdOverride from by-tenant-published calls; use systemQuery with the tenant id, as the seo feature does.

title: Branding exports removed from managed-pages
detail: `BRANDING_QN`, `MANAGED_PAGES_CSS_FEATURE` and `createManagedPagesCssFeature` are no longer exported from managed-pages. Branding config, query and screen live in the branding feature, and custom CSS is gated by `createBrandingCssFeature()`.
migration: Import `BRANDING_QN` from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/branding and replace `createManagedPagesCssFeature()` with `createBrandingCssFeature()` next to `createBrandingFeature({ allowCustomCss })`. `MANAGED_PAGES_CSS_FEATURE` is replaced by `BRANDING_CSS_FEATURE` from the same branding subpath.

title: page mask on the editor workbench with a live preview of the unsaved body
managed-pages client bundle no longer loads tiptap at start
The public render caches a sanitized document body per page version
A managed page body is Markdown or an editor document, edited in the document editor
detail: The page entity has a new field bodyFormat ("markdown" or "document", default markdown). Pages and events from before the field read as markdown and render unchanged. A document body is HTML from the template-resolver document editor; page create, update and managed-pages:write:set check it with sanitizeDocumentHtml and store the rebuilt HTML and answer a rejected body with field errors on body (i18n key managed-pages.errors.document.rejected, new in all locale packages). The public render sanitizes a document body again and serves an empty body, with a logged warning, when a stored one fails. managed-pages:write:set takes an optional bodyFormat; omitting it sets markdown, it does not preserve the stored format. The page-edit screen no longer has a body textarea: its body section is the extension section managed-pages:page-body (PAGE_BODY_EXTENSION_NAME), which opens a Markdown body converted to HTML, shows a warning for what the conversion drops (images, block quotes, code, headings below level 3, relative links) and writes body and bodyFormat "document" only after the first edit. The ETag of the public page includes bodyFormat. seedPage takes an optional bodyFormat and throws on a rejected document body.
migration: Run `kumiko-schema generate` and apply the migration; read_pages gets a bodyFormat column with default 'markdown', no rebuild is needed. Mount `managedPagesClient()` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/managed-pages/web` in createKumikoApp({ clientFeatures }); without it the body section of page-edit shows the missing-component placeholder. Apps that replaced page-edit with their own screen keep the textarea and send no bodyFormat, so their pages stay markdown.
